Name: HAL

Box Tagline: With Lasers You Swivel and Elevate

The HAL was discontinued in 1984. In 1984, the HAL was repackaged with the VAMP Attack Jeep in a special Sears exclusive VAMP & HAL boxed set. The HAL was available from Hasbro Direct via mail-away offers from 1984 until 1990.

In 1994 the mail-order APC was availabile as the convention exclusive 'CUDA [Coastal Unit Defense Amphibious Transport].  The only differences between the APC and 'CUDA are the box packaging and the inclusion of leftover stock of Cutter (v3) (1993) as the driver.

Name: Cobra Venom Cycle
Release Notes: The Cobra Venom Cycle (Repaint) was released carded in U.S. toy stores in 2003.  It was part of the Spy Troops line and came with the figure, Cobra Viper (v10).  This vehicle was created using the mold from the original Cobra Venom Cycle (2003).

Name: Conquest of Cobra Mountain
Box Tagline: Capture the COBRA mountain fortress and change it into a G.I. JOE bunker!
Release Notes: The Conquest of Cobra Mountain was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with Shipwreck (v7) in 2003. The Conquest of Cobra Mountain uses a heavily modified mold from the Star Wars: Attack of the Clones Geonosis Battle Arena for the two floor plates and the door section. The playset featured nine firing missiles, interchangable flags, a Cobra Throne that could be changed to a G.I.Joe control room, an "exploding" wall area, and more.

Name: Crimson Command Copter
Box Tagline: Joystick raises gun and wings and fires 10 missiles!
Release Notes: The Crimson Command Copter was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with Tomax (v4) and Xamot (v4) in 2003. The helicopter featured ten firing missiles activated by a pull-down joystick, a Sound Attack Weapon, a light-up gun, rolling wheels, sliding doors, an opening cockpit, and a trigger that rotates the rotors and actives a helicopter sound. The Crimson Command Copter used a mold modified from the Night Attack Chopper (2002) and the Night Attack Chopper (Desert) (2003).

Name: Desert Coyote
Release Notes: The Desert Coyote was released carded in U.S. toy stores with the pilot Double Clutch in 2003. The Desert Coyote featured Action Attack technology, a firing missile, and a rotating gunner station. A thumb wheel located on the back of the vehicle operated the turret motion and weapon sound (with switch in either position) while the motion of the rear wheels activated the vehicle sound (only with switch in "play" position). The Desert Coyote was released boxed in U.S. stores in 2004 as part of the Valor vs. Venom line.   The vehicle was stripped of the Sound Attack Technology, had different instructions, and did not include blueprints. Double Clutch was included with the boxed version also.

Name: Gun Station
Release Notes: The Gun Station was released carded in U.S. toy stores in 2003.  It was part of the Spy Troops line and came with the figure, Big Brawler. The Gun Station features three firing missiles and rotating action. The Gun Station was repainted in 2004 to make the Gun Station.

Name: Hoverstrike
Release Notes: The Hoverstrike was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the pilot Mirage (v4) in 2003.  The Hoverstrike was a working remote controlled hovercraft that fired six missiles.  The Hoverstrike came with either a 27 or 49 Mhz Frequency remote control.

Name: Missile Storm Copter
Release Notes:
The Missile Storm Copter was released carded in U.S. toy stores with the pilot Wild Bill (v6) in 2003.  The Missile Storm Copter featured Sound Attack technology and a firing missile.  Many parts on the Missile Storm Copter were originally used in the Cobra F.A.N.G. 3.
	
The Missile Storm Copter was released boxed in U.S. stores in 2004 as part of the Valor vs. Venom line.   The vehicle was stripped of the Sound Attack Technology, had different instructions, and did not include blueprints. Wild Bill (v6) was included with the boxed version also.

Name: MUV
Release Notes: The MUV is a remote controlled vehicle and was released boxed in U.S. toy stores in 2003.  It was part of the Spy Troops line and came with the figure, Beachhead (v4).

Name: Night Attack Chopper
Release Notes: The Night Attack Chopper was released boxed in U.S. toy stores in 2002. It was available again in 2003 as part of the Spy Troops line. It was repackaged in a Spy Troops box and repainted in Desert Camouflage.

Name: Patriot Grizzly Tank
Release Notes: The Patriot Grizzly Tank was released boxed in U.S. toy stores in 2003. The Patriot Grizzly Tank was part of the Spy Troops line and featured Action Attack Technology. Push the tank for engine sounds, or flip down a joystick to to activate sounds, rotate turrets, or fire missiles from the motorized launcher (2 C batteries required, not included).

Name: Polar Blast
Release Notes: The Polar Blast was released carded in U.S. toy stores with the driver Snow Serpent (v6) in 2003. The Polar Blast was part of the SpyTroops line and featured Action Attack Technology.  Move the front gun or handle bars to hear weapons sounds, press trigger to launch missile and make gunner's seat recoil, or move vehicle for engine sounds.

Name: Road Rebel
Release Notes: The Road Rebel was released carded in U.S. toy stores in 2003.  It was part of the Spy Troops line and came with the figure, Big Ben (v6).

Name: Sky Sweeper Jet
Release Notes: The Sky Sweeper Jet was released boxed in U.S. toy stores in 2003.  The Sky Sweeper Jet was part of the Spy Troops line and features Sound Attack Technology. The Sky Sweeper Jet was was repainted in 2004 and released again as the Sky Sweeper Jet.

Name: Smoke Screen Transport
Release Notes: The Smoke Screen Transport was released boxed in U.S. toy stores in 2003.  The Smoke Screen Transport was part of the Spy Troops line and features Sound Attack Technology, a removable spy craft, and firing missiles. The Smoke Screen Transport was also available in 2004 as part of the Costco Battle in a Box Exclusive set.

Name: Split Fire
Box Tagline: Assault truck with pivoting gun stations!
Release Notes: The Split Fire was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the pilot Rampage (v2) in 2003.  The Split Fire featured "Action Attack", with two firing missiles, engine sounds, and a handle that rotated the gun stations and activated firing sounds.

Name: Wave Crusher
Release Notes: The Wave Crusher was released carded in U.S. toy stores in 2003.  It was part of the Spy Troops line and came with the figure, Depth Charge. The Wave Crusher is able to transform from a G.I.Joe water Sled to a Cobra jet ski, and features a firing missile.

Name: Cobra C.A.T. II
Release Notes: The Cobra C.A.T. II was released boxed with the driver Crimson Guard Immortal (v2) in 2003. The Cobra C.A.T. II was a K-B Toys exclusive. As with the original Crimson Attack Tank (1985), the Cobra C.A.T. II was created using the mold of the MOBAT (1982).

Name: A.W.E. Striker
Box Tagline: Try Me! Press Button to Hear Sounds!
Release Notes: The A.W.E. Striker was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the pilot Dial-Tone (v6) in 2003.  The A.W.E. Striker was a Toys R Us Exclusive, and featured Sound Attack Technology.

Name: Conquest X-30
Release Notes: The Conquest X-30 was created using the same mold as the original 1986 Conquest X-30.  Some modifications were made to include the Sound Attack Weapon.

Name: Mobile Command Center
Box Tagline: Changes from a command center to mobile command vehicle
Release Notes: The Mobile Command Center was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with Leatherneck (v4) in 2003.  The Mobile Command Center was a Toys R Us exclusive. The Mobile Command Center reuses the mold from the original Mobile Command Center (1987), with only a slight difference in colors. The playset changed from a command center to mobile command vehicle, and featured a service bay with fold-out ramp and a command bay.

Name: Snow Cat
Release Notes: The Snow Cat was released boxed as a Toys R Us exclusive in 2003. It was part of the Spy Troops line and came with the figure, Frostbite (v7). The Snow Cat mold was first used in 1985 to create the original Snow Cat and again in 1988 to create the Tiger Force Tiger Cat.

Name: Cobra HISS Tank IIB
Subtitle: HIGH SPEED SENTRY
Release Notes: The Cobra HISS Tank IIB  was released as a 2003 Convention exclusive. The mold was originally used in 1989 to create the Cobra H.I.S.S. II Tank.

Name: Torpedo Submarine
Release Notes: The Torpedo Submarine was released as a 2003 Convention attendee exclusive.  Attendees who purchased the American Hero Set received three submarines per box set. The mold was originally used in 1990 to create the one-man sidesubs for the Cobra Hammerhead.

Name: Air Assault
Release Notes: The Air Assault was released carded in U.S. toy stores in 2004, originally as a Target exclusive.

Name: Battle Hornet
Release Notes: The Battle Hornet was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the driver Neo-Viper (v8) in 2004. Battle Hornet was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and featured firing missiles, dropping bombs, landing gear that folded in at the touch of a button, and numerous sounds.  The Battle Hornet used 2 AAA batteries, included.

Name: Defense Mech
Release Notes: The Defense Mech was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the driver Leatherneck (v5) in 2004. The Defense Mech was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and features an opening canopy, firing missiles, movable arms and legs, and a cannon with lights and sounds.  The Defense Mech is articulated at the hips, knees, shoulders, and the left elbow.

Name: Gun Station
Release Notes: The Gun Station was released carded in U.S. toy stores in 2004, originally as a Target exclusive.  It was part of the Valor vs Venom line and came with the figure, Dart. The Gun Station features three firing missiles and rotating action and is a repaint of the original Gun Station.

Name: Ice Sabre
Release Notes: The Ice Sabre was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the driver Frostbite (v8) in 2004. The Ice Sabre was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and features an opening canopy, a pop-up rotating turret that fires four missiles, and pivoting front skis.

Name: Jungle Strike Humvee
Release Notes: The Jungle Strike Humvee was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the driver Rollbar in 2004. The Jungle Strike Humvee was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and featured rolling wheels, opening doors, hood and trunk, and interchangeable roof weapons with a firing missile.

Name: Neutralizer
Release Notes: The Neutralizer was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the driver Backblast (v3) in 2004. Neutralizer was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and featured extendable cannons and firing missiles.

Name: Night Adder
Release Notes: The Night Adder was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the pilot Wild Weasel (v3) in 2004. The Night Adder was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and features an opening canopy, firing missile, sliding wing tips, and a handle that folds down and activates the moving turret and the light up reciprocating cannons.

Name: Night Force Grizzly Tank
Release Notes: The Night Force Grizzly Tank was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the driver Wild Bill (v6) in 2004. The Night Force Grizzly Tank was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and featured and featured Action Attack Technology. Push the tank for engine sounds, or flip down a joystick to to activate sounds, rotate turrets, or fire missiles from the motorized launcher (2 C batteries required, not included. The Night Force Grizzly Tank was made using the same mold as the Patriot Grizzly Tank (2003).

Name: Ninja Lightning Cycle
Release Notes: The Ninja Lightning Cycle was released carded in U.S. toy stores in 2004, originally as a Target exclusive.  It was part of the Valor vs Venom line and came with the figure, Storm Shadow. The Ninja Lightning Cycle features a firing missile, working kickstand, and rotating tires and was a repainted to make the Ninja Lightning Cycle (2004).

Name: Ninja Lightning Cycle
Release Notes: The Ninja Lightning Cycle was released carded in U.S. toy stores in 2004.  It was part of the Valor vs Venom line and came with the figure, Snake Eyes. The Ninja Lightning Cycle features a firing missile, working kickstand, and rotating tires and was a repaint of the Ninja Lightning Cycle (2004).

Name: Piranha Attack Boat
Release Notes: The Piranha Attack Boat was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the pilot Shipwreck (v8) in 2004. The Piranha Attack Boat was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and features twin firing torpedo launchers, a working motor, and a knob that swivels the gun emplacements.  The Piranha Attack Boat also floats on water. The Piranha Attack Boat requires 2 AA batteries (not included) to work the engines.

Name: Pulverizer
Release Notes: The Pulverizer was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the driver Ghost Bear in 2004. The Pulverizer was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and features an opening canopy, firing missile, movable arms and legs, and a spring shut claw with lights and sounds. The Pulverizer is articulated at the hips and shoulders.

Name: Quickstrike
Release Notes: The Quickstrike was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the driver Sgt. Bazooka in 2004. The Quickstrike was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and features an opening canopy, rotating turret, and a lift-up, firing missile launcher.

Name: Sky Sweeper Jet
Release Notes: The Sky Sweeper Jet was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the driver Sgt. Airborne (v2) in 2004. The Sky Sweeper Jet was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and features an opening canopy, extending wings and tail, firing missiles, retractable landing gear, and a hidden spy plane.

Name: Sting Raider
Release Notes: The Sting Raider was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the driver Electric EEL (v2) in 2004. The Sting Raider was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and features an opening canopy, pivoting engines with movable fan blades, a button activated grabber claw, fold-up wing tips, expanding wings, and firing missiles.

Name: Thunderwing Jet
Release Notes: The Thunderwing Jet was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the driver Slip Stream (v3) in 2004. The Thunderwing Jet was also available at Toys R Us in 2004 with an additional Ace (v6) figure. Thunderwing Jet was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and featured the following: Control handle folds down or up into the belly of the plane 10 top loading missiles that are launched from a button on the handle, firing the missiles out of the front of the plane 4 trigger activated dropping bombs 11 phrases, including Push it Up, Switching to bombs, Bombs away, Target destroyed, Switching to missiles, Missile away, Cobra goin' down, Go tactical, Break right, Break left, and Cobra bearing 225. Retractable landing gear Opening canopy Lights and sounds (engine, bombs, missiles) Rear exhaust ports double as targeting sensors, can be switched from bomb to missile mode

Name: Tiger Storm Copter
Release Notes: The Tiger Storm Copter was released carded in 2004 with Wild Bill (v8), Recondo (v4), Sand Viper (v3), and a 16 page Valor vs Venom Comic Book, written by Larry Hama. The Tiger Storm Copter was a repaint of the Missile Storm Copter (2003), which used many parts from the Cobra F.A.N.G. 3 (2002). The Tiger Storm Copter featured Sound Attack technology and a firing missile.

Name: Tigerhawk
Release Notes: The Tigerhawk jet was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the pilot Ace (v6) in 2004. The Tigerhawk was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and features an opening canopy, bomb dropping action and sounds, barrel roll action and sounds, and folding wing tips.

Name: Tigerhawk
Release Notes: The Tigerhawk (repaint) was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the driver Ace (v7) in 2004. The Tigerhawk (repaint) was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and featured an opening canopy, bomb dropping action and sounds, barrel roll action and sounds, and folding wing tips. This Tigerhawk was a repaint of the Tigerhawk released earlier in 2004.

Name: Venom Striker
Release Notes: The Venom Striker was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the driver Cobra C.L.A.W.S. (v5) in 2004. The Venom Striker was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and features laser weapon sounds, a firing missile, swiveling gun platform, and rolling wheels. The Venom Striker uses a modified mold of the Assault Quad (2002).

Name: Operation Crimson Sabotage
Driver / Pilot: CRIMSON GUARD (v3); CRIMSON GUARD (v4); CRIMSON GUARD (v5)
Release Notes: The Operation Crimson Sabotage set was released boxed with Crimson Guard (v3), Crimson Guard (v4), and Crimson Guard (v5) in 2004 and was a KB Toys exclusive. The Operation Crimson Sabotage set was part of the Valor vs. Venom line, and featured an opening cockpit, rotating gun turret, and an anti-aircraft gun that could be attached to the tow hook.

Name: A.P.C. Transport
Release Notes: The A.P.C. Transport was released boxed with three Cobra B.A.T.s (v7) in 2004. The A.P.C. Transport was part of the Valor vs. Venom line, held at least twenty-two figures, featured a raising and firing launcher, and was a Toys R Us exclusive. The A.P.C. Transport was a repaint of the Monster Blaster A.P.C. (1993).

Name: V.A.M.P. with Twin Battle Gun
Subtitle: MULTI-PURPOSE ATTACK VEHICLE
Release Notes: The V.A.M.P. with Twin Battle Gun was released boxed with Chief Torpedo v2, Big Brawler v4, and a reissued Pathfinder v2 (2001) in 2004 and was a Toys R Us exclusive. The V.A.M.P. with Twin Battle Gun was part of the Valor vs. Venom line, featured removable ammo panels, rotating gun barrels, and a firing rocket launcher. The V.A.M.P. was created using the mold of the Desert Striker (2001), a heavily re-worked vehicle created from the original V.A.M.P. (1982). The Twin Battle Gun was created from the mold of the Whirlwind [Twin Battle Gun] (1983).

Name: Dreadnok Cycle
Release Notes:
The Convention Dreadnok Cycle was released as a 2004 Convention Exclusive.  
The mold and labels were originally used in 1987 to create the original Dreadnok Cycle. The spring launcher and missile molds were originally used in 
1990 as part of the Hammerhead. The turret platform has been re-tooled to allow for the missiles to attach to the sides rather than the underside. Additional note: The blueprints provided with the 2004 convention vehicles are photocopies of the blueprints released with the original vehicles and will thus be cross linked with
those original blueprints rather than using images of the photocopies.

Name: Dreadnok Stun
Release Notes:
The Convention Dreadnok Stun was released as a 2004 Convention Exclusive. The majority of the mold was originally used in 1986 to create the original Stun. 
The hubcaps for the Convention Dreadnok Stun were re-tooled to show the Dreadnok logo in place of the Cobra Symbol. Additional note: The blueprints provided with the 2004 convention vehicles are photocopies of the blueprints released with the original vehicles and will thus be cross linked with
those original blueprints rather than using images of the photocopies.

Name: Tiger-Ray Hydrofoil
Release Notes:
The Convention Tiger-Ray Hydrofoil was released as a 2004 Convention Exclusive. The mold was originally used in 1985 to create the original Moray Hydrofoil, and later re-released in 1989 to create the Night Ray. Additional note: The blueprints provided with the 2004 convention vehicles are photocopies of the blueprints released with the original vehicles and will thus be cross linked with
those original blueprints rather than using images of the photocopies.

Name: Battle in a Box
Category: G.I.Joe and Cobra Boxed Sets (Costco Exclusive)
Subtitle: BATTLE IN A BOX (SMOKE SCREEN TRANSPORT AND COBRA RINGNECK)
Driver / Pilot: DART (v2); NUNCHUK (v4); TUNNEL RAT (v4); COBRA COILS (v2); PIT VIPER (v1); TELE-VIPER (v3)
Release Notes: The Battle in a Box (Smoke Screen Transport and Cobra Ringneck) was released in 2004 as a Costco Exclusive. The set included the Smoke Screen Transport and Cobra Ringneck vehicles, and the figures of Dart (v2), Nunchuk (v4), Tunnel Rat (v4), Cobra Coils (v2), Pit Viper, and Tele-Viper (v3).

Name: Assault Quad
Category: G.I.Joe and Cobra Boxed Sets (K-Mart Exclusive)
Release Notes: The Assault Quad (Operation: Avalanche) was released boxed in U.S. toy stores as part of the K-Mart Exclusive Operation: Avalanche boxed set.  The set included the Assault Quad, two Air Assault gliders, Snake Eyes (v13), Dusty (v7), Iron Grenadiers (v2), and Storm Shadow (v13). The Assault Quad (Operation: Avalanche) was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and featured a firing missile, swiveling gun platform, and rolling wheels. The Assault Quad (Operation: Avalanche) uses the mold of the Assault Quad (2002) with a gun from the Venom Striker (2004).

Name: Operation: Avalanche
Category: G.I.Joe and Cobra Boxed Sets (K-Mart Exclusive)
Driver / Pilot: DUSTY (v7); IRON GRENADIER (v2); SNAKE EYES (v13); STORM SHADOW (v13)
Release Notes: Operation: Avalanche was released in 2004 as a K-Mart Exclusive. The set included the Assault Quad and two Air Assault vehicles, and the figures of Snake Eyes (v13), Dusty (v7), Iron Grenadiers (v2), and Storm Shadow (v13).

Name: Air Assault
Release Notes: The Air Assault was released carded in U.S. toy stores in 2005. It was part of the Valor vs Venom line and came with the figure, Sand Viper. The Air Assault was a repaint of the original Air Assault.

Name: Cobra H.I.S.S.
Release Notes: The Cobra H.I.S.S. was released boxed in U.S. toy stores in 2005 as part of the Valor vs Venom line. The box included the driver, Pit Viper (v2). The H.I.S.S. featured an extending attack mode, three firing missiles, and retractable turret cannons. It was retooled from the Cobra Hiss IV (2002) with an entirely new gun turret.

Name: Desert Coyote
Release Notes:
The Desert Coyote was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the pilot Recondo (v5) in 2005. The Desert 
Coyote featured Action Attack technology, a firing missile, and a rotating gunner station. A thumb wheel located on the back of the vehicle operated the turret motion.

Name: Desert Humvee
Release Notes: The Desert Humvee was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the driver Duke in late 2004, but is considered a 2005 product by Hasbro. The Desert Humvee was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and featured rolling wheels, opening doors, hood, and trunk, and interchangeable roof weapons with a firing missile.

Name: Night Adder
Release Notes: The Night Adder (Repaint) was released boxed in U.S. toy stores with the pilot Wild Weasel (v5) in late 2004, but is considered a 2005 product by Hasbro. The Night Adder was part of the Valor vs. Venom line and features an opening canopy, firing missile, sliding wing tips, and a handle that folds down and activates the moving turret and the light up reciprocating cannons.

Name: Ninja Lightning Cycle
Release Notes: The Ninja Lightning Cycle was released carded in U.S. toy stores in 2005. It was part of the Valor vs Venom line and came with the figure, Kamakura. The Ninja Lightning Cycle features a firing missile, working kickstand, and rotating tires and was a repaint of the Ninja Lightning Cycle (2004).

Name: Venomization Chamber
Release Notes: The Venomization Chamber was released boxed in U.S. toy stores in 2005. It was part of the Valor vs Venom line and came with the figure, Venomous Maximus. The Venomization Chamber featured an action ability to transform one figure into another and included a victim. This process featured lights, sounds, and a rotating venomization pod. Click here for a video of the venomization process.

Name: Wave Crusher
Release Notes: The Wave Crusher was released carded in U.S. toy stores in 2005. It was part of the Valor vs Venom line and came with the figure, Depth Charge. The Wave Crusher is able to transform from a water sled to a jet ski,  and features a firing missile.

Name: Cobra H.I.S.S.
Release Notes: The Cobra H.I.S.S. was released boxed as an online and Toys R Us exclusive with the driver Night Creeper (v10) in 2005. The Cobra H.I.S.S. features eight firing missiles, removable front guns, opening canopy, pivoting gun turret, and opening sides to allow access to troop transport areas.

Name: Night Ops Humvee
Box Tagline: Includes: Vehicle, Weapons, Accessories and Rollbar Figure
Release Notes: The Night Ops Humvee was released boxed as an online exclusive with the driver Rollbar (v2) in 2005. The Night Ops Humvee features an opening hood, a flip-down brushguard, opening doors, and interchangeable weapons.

Name: R.H.I.N.O.
Subtitle: RAPID HELI-INTEGRATED NEUTRALIZING OFFENSIVE VEHICLE
Box Tagline: Includes: Vehicle, Helicopter, Weapons, Missiles and Cannonball Figure.
Release Notes: The R.H.I.N.O. Rapid Heli-Integrated Neutralizing Offensive Vehicle was released boxed as an online exclusive with the driver Cannonball in 2005. The R.H.I.N.O. Rapid Heli-Integrated Neutralizing Offensive Vehicle has the following features: Deployable Secret Helicopter Slow Rise Helipad Opening Canopy Fold Out Wings Weapons Ports Missile-Firing Launchers can be Mounted in Different Places Missiles Opening Hatches Spring Open Side Hatch

Name: R.O.C.C.
Subtitle: ROLLING OPERATIONS COMMAND CENTER
Box Tagline: Includes: Car, Trailer, Jet, Missiles and Long Range Figure.
Release Notes: The R.O.C.C. Rolling Operations Command Center was released boxed as an online exclusive with the driver Long Range (v2) in 2005. The R.O.C.C. Rolling Operations Command Center has the following features: Moveable Robotic Arm with Grabber Claw Hidden Launcher Fires 8 Missiles Fold Down Driver's Windscreen Cab Separates from Trailer Fold Down Ramps Open Trailer to Reveal Command Center Jet with Opening Canopy Jet Attaches to Launch Platform Moveable Gun Turret Escape Tube Sliding Elevator

Name: G.I. Joe Moray Hydrofoil
Subtitle: WITH FLINT AND BEACHHEAD
Release Notes: The G.I. Joe Moray Hydrofoil was released boxed as a Toys R Us exclusive with the pilots Flint (v9) and Beachhead (v6) in 2005.

Name: Cobra Stealth Moray
Release Notes: The Cobra Hydrofoil was released as a 2005 Convention exclusive. The 2005 Hydrofoil was in essence a "recoloring" of the 2004 Convention Tiger-Ray Hydrofoil. The 2005 Hydrofoil was sold as an extra deck along with a MIB 2004 Convention Tiger-Ray Hydrofoil.

Name: Iron Grenadier Stealth AGP
Subtitle: ANTI-GRAVITY POD
Release Notes: The Iron Grenadier Stealth AGP was released as a 2005 Convention exclusive.

Name: Iron Mech
Release Notes: The Iron Mech was released as a 2005 Convention exclusive.

Name: Steel Brigade Skyhawk
Release Notes: The Steel Brigade Skyhawk was released as a 2005 Convention exclusive, bagged as a set of three.

Name: Ninja Battles
Driver / Pilot: BLACK DRAGON NINJA (v2); SHADOW STRIKE (v1); SNAKE EYES (v22); STORM SHADOW (v17); TIGER CLAW (v1)
Release Notes:
The Ninja Battles play set was released in late 2004, but is considered a 2005 product by Hasbro. The play set featured collapsible pillars.
The Ninja Battles boxed set included the play set shown below, as well as a Ninja Battles DVD, Ninja Battles Comic Book, Black Dragon Ninja (v2), Shadow Strike, Snake Eyes (v22), Storm Shadow (v17), and Tiger Claw.

Name: Ice Sabre
Box Tagline: Includes: Vehicle, Missiles and Frostbite Figure.
Release Notes: The Ice Sabre was released as part of the DTC 2006 Wave 1 along with the driver Frostbite (v11) in 2006. The Ice Sabre features an opening canopy, a pop-up rotating turret that fires four missiles, and pivoting front skis.

Name: Cobra Ferret ATV
Subtitle: ALL TERRAIN VEHICLE
Release Notes: The Cobra Ferret ATV was released in a two-pack with the Coil Ferret ATV as a 2006 Convention exclusive, limited to 800 sets.

Name: Coil Ferret ATV
Subtitle: ALL TERRAIN VEHICLE
Release Notes: The Coil Ferret ATV was released in a two-pack with the Cobra Ferret ATV as a 2006 Convention exclusive.

Name: Renegade's Warthog APV
Subtitle: ARMORED PERSONNEL VEHICLE
Release Notes: The Desert Camouflage Warthog was released as a 2006 Convention exclusive.

Name: Sgt. Slaughter's Armadillo
Release Notes: Sgt. Slaughter's Armadillo was released as a 2006 Convention exclusive.

Name: VAMP Mark V
Subtitle: VEHICLE ATTACK: MULTI-PURPOSE
Release Notes: The VAMP Mark V was released as a 2007 Convention exclusive.

Name: A.W.E. Striker
Subtitle: WITH CRANKCASE
Release Notes: The A.W.E. Striker was first released boxed in U.S. toy stores as part of the Target-exclusive "Attack on Cobra Island" wave of vehicles in  2008. It included the driver, Crankcase (v2).

Name: Cobra Flight Pod
Subtitle: ULTIMATE BATTLE PACK
Release Notes: The Cobra Flight Pod was released boxed with the Cobra H.I.S.S. Tank and the MOBAT in the Target Exclusive Ultimate Battle Pack in 2008. The package also included the drivers, Cobra Commander (v37), H.I.S.S. Driver (v3), and Steeler (v5), as well as Cobra Vehicle Gunner, Destro (v21), Short-Fuze (v6), and Sgt. Stalker (v11).

Name: Cobra H.I.S.S.
Subtitle: WITH COBRA DRIVER
Release Notes: The Cobra H.I.S.S. was first released boxed in U.S. toy stores as part of the Target-exclusive "Attack on Cobra Island" wave of vehicles in 2008. It included the driver, Cobra Driver.

Name: Cobra H.I.S.S. Tank
Subtitle: ULTIMATE BATTLE PACK
Release Notes: The Cobra H.I.S.S. Tank was released boxed with the Cobra Flight Pod and the MOBAT in the Target Exclusive Ultimate Battle Pack in 2008. The package also included the drivers, Cobra Commander (v37), H.I.S.S. Driver (v3), and Steeler (v5), as well as Cobra Vehicle Gunner, Destro (v21), Short-Fuze (v6), and Sgt. Stalker (v11).

Name: Cobra Rattler
Release Notes: The Cobra Rattler was released in 2008 in the second wave of Target-exclusive vehicles. It included the driver, Wild Weasel (v6).

Name: Conquest X-30
Release Notes: The Conquest X-30 was released in 2008 in the second wave of Target-exclusive vehicles. It included the driver, Lt. Slip Stream.

Name: M.A.S.S. Device

The Weather Dominator from Set 2 could attach to the Generator, and the Control Cube from Set 4 could attach to the Transport Chassis. Additionally, three unique M.A.S.S. element containers were released with individually carded figures.  Though compatible with this vehicle, they are not necessary to consider this vehicle complete as the blueprints do not show them. The element containers were available with Cobra Commander (v31) (2008), Tripwire (v5) (2008), and Cobra Diver (2008).
